points.title: 早年教育
points.description: 西塞罗出生于意大利中部的阿尔皮努姆，这是一个距离罗马约100公里的城镇。虽然出身于骑士阶层，但并非最显赫的贵族家庭。他的父亲是一位富裕的乡绅，重视教育，聘请了当时最好的希腊教师为西塞罗和弟弟昆图斯授课。这段时期，西塞罗接受了系统的古典教育，学习了修辞学、哲学和文学，为他日后成为罗马最伟大的演说家和作家奠定了基础。他特别崇拜希腊哲学家和演说家的思想，这影响了他的整个政治生涯。
points.descriptionEn: Cicero was born in Arpinum, a town in central Italy about 100 kilometers from Rome. Although from the equestrian class rather than the highest nobility, his father was a wealthy landowner who valued education and hired the best Greek tutors for Cicero and his brother Quintus. During this period, Cicero received a comprehensive classical education in rhetoric, philosophy, and literature, which laid the foundation for his later career as Rome's greatest orator and writer. He particularly admired the works of Greek philosophers and orators, which influenced his entire political career.

points.title: 法律与政治启蒙
points.description: 西塞罗来到罗马接受更高等的教育，师从当时著名的法学家斯凯沃拉和哲学家菲洛。他迅速展现出非凡的才华，特别是在法律和修辞学方面。在此期间，他目睹了同盟者战争(公元前91-88年)和苏拉的内战，这些动荡的政治事件深刻影响了他对共和国制度的看法。西塞罗通过精湛的辩护技巧在法庭上崭露头角，成功为多位知名人物辩护，积累了政治资本和人脉。他还开始写作早期的法律著作，并结识了当时罗马知识界的精英人物。
points.descriptionEn: Cicero came to Rome for higher education, studying under the famous jurist Scaevola and the philosopher Philo. He quickly demonstrated exceptional talent, particularly in law and rhetoric. During this time, he witnessed the Social War (91-88 BC) and Sulla's civil war, which profoundly influenced his views on the republican system. Cicero emerged as a rising star in the courts with his brilliant defense techniques, successfully representing several prominent figures and accumulating political capital and connections. He also began writing his early legal works and met the intellectual elite of Rome.

points.title: 哲学深造
points.description: 在完成法律学业后，西塞罗前往希腊世界深造，先后在雅典和罗德岛学习哲学。在雅典，他追随柏拉图学园的哲学家学习，深入研究了柏拉图、亚里士多德等希腊哲学家的思想。在罗德岛，他向著名演说家阿波罗尼乌斯学习修辞学技巧。这段经历使西塞罗不仅吸收了希腊哲学的精髓，还形成了自己独特的思想体系。他开始思考如何将希腊哲学思想与罗马传统相结合，为日后将希腊哲学介绍到罗马并发展罗马哲学奠定了基础。同时，他也完善了自己的演说风格，融合了希腊修辞学的严谨与罗马演说的激情。
points.descriptionEn: After completing his legal studies, Cicero traveled to the Greek world for further education, studying in Athens and Rhodes. In Athens, he followed the Platonic Academy philosophers and deeply studied the works of Greek philosophers like Plato and Aristotle. In Rhodes, he studied rhetoric techniques under the famous orator Apollonius. This experience allowed Cicero not only to absorb the essence of Greek philosophy but also to develop his own unique philosophical system. He began contemplating how to combine Greek philosophical thought with Roman traditions, laying the foundation for his later work in introducing Greek philosophy to Rome and developing Roman philosophy. At the same time, he perfected his oratorical style, combining the rigor of Greek rhetoric with the passion of Roman oratory.

points.title: 政治崛起
points.description: 回到罗马后，西塞罗的政治生涯迅速上升。他凭借出色的法律才能和演说技巧，在法庭上取得了一系列成功，包括为西西里行省的官员辩护，赢得了广泛声誉。公元前70年，他在维勒斯案中揭露了前总督的腐败，成为罗马公众的英雄。公元前63年，西塞罗当选为执政官，达到了政治生涯的顶峰。作为执政官，他挫败了喀提林阴谋，拯救了共和国，因此获得了'国父'(Pater Patriae)的称号。这一时期，他创作了多部重要的政治和哲学著作，包括《论演说家》和《论共和国》，奠定了他在罗马思想史上的地位。
points.descriptionEn: After returning to Rome, Cicero's political career rose rapidly. With his exceptional legal talent and oratory skills, he achieved a series of successes in the courts, including defending officials of the Sicilian province, winning widespread reputation. In 70 BC, he exposed the corruption of the former governor Verres in the Verres case, becoming a hero to the Roman public. In 63 BC, Cicero was elected consul, reaching the pinnacle of his political career. As consul, he thwarted the Catilinarian conspiracy and saved the republic, earning the title 'Father of the Fatherland' (Pater Patriae). During this period, he wrote several important political and philosophical works, including 'De Oratore' and 'De Re Publica', establishing his place in Roman intellectual history.

points.title: 流放与回归
points.description: 尽管西塞罗在挫败喀提林阴谋后声望达到顶点，但他的政治立场使他得罪了庞培和克拉苏等权贵。公元前58年，在保民官克洛狄乌斯的推动下，西塞罗因'处死公民未经审判'的罪名被流放到希腊。在流放期间，西塞罗继续写作，完成了《论命运》和《论老年》等哲学著作。公元前57年，在元老院和民众的支持下，西塞罗被允许返回罗马，受到热烈欢迎。回归后，他继续积极参与政治，试图在庞培、凯撒和克拉苏之间维持共和国的平衡，但最终未能阻止内战的爆发。这一时期，他的政治理想与残酷的现实之间的矛盾日益凸显。
points.descriptionEn: Despite reaching the peak of his reputation after thwarting the Catilinarian conspiracy, Cicero's political stance earned him the enmity of powerful figures like Pompey and Crassus. In 58 BC, driven by the tribune Clodius, Cicero was exiled to Greece on charges of 'executing citizens without trial.' During his exile, Cicero continued writing, completing philosophical works such as 'De Fato' and 'De Senectute.' In 57 BC, with the support of the Senate and people, Cicero was allowed to return to Rome, receiving a warm welcome. After his return, he continued to actively participate in politics, attempting to maintain the balance of the republic between Pompey, Caesar, and Crassus, but ultimately failed to prevent the outbreak of civil war. During this period, the contradiction between his political ideals and the harsh reality became increasingly apparent.

points.title: 内战与遇害
points.description: 凯撒与庞培之间的内战爆发后，西塞罗最初支持庞培，但在法萨卢斯战役后转向与凯撒和解。凯撒被刺杀后，西塞罗试图恢复共和制，发表了一系列著名的反安东尼演说(《腓力皮克》)，谴责安东尼的独裁倾向。然而，这些演说激怒了安东尼和屋大维组成的后三头同盟。公元前43年，西塞罗被列入 proscription名单(追杀名单)，在逃亡途中被安东尼的士兵捕获并处死。他的头颅和双手被送到罗马，展示在演讲台上，这是对他作为演说家身份的终极羞辱。西塞罗之死标志着罗马共和传统的终结，他的著作和思想却得以保存，对后世产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: After the outbreak of civil war between Caesar and Pompey, Cicero initially supported Pompey but later reconciled with Caesar after the Battle of Pharsalus. After Caesar's assassination, Cicero attempted to restore the republic, delivering a series of famous anti-Antony speeches (Philippics) condemning Antony's dictatorial tendencies. However, these speeches angered the Second Triumvirate formed by Antony and Octavian. In 43 BC, Cicero was placed on the proscription list and was captured and executed by Antony's soldiers while fleeing. His head and hands were sent to Rome and displayed on the Rostra, the ultimate humiliation for him as an orator. Cicero's death marked the end of the Roman republican tradition, yet his writings and thoughts survived, exerting profound influence on later generations.

supporter.zh: 西塞罗被尊为罗马最伟大的演说家、哲学家和政治家之一。他捍卫共和制度，反对独裁，为罗马法治传统奠定了基础。他将希腊哲学思想引入罗马，创造了拉丁哲学语言，使西方文明得以传承。他的著作《论共和国》和《论法律》成为政治理论的经典，影响了后世无数思想家。西塞罗坚持道德原则，即使在政治危机中也保持独立思考，体现了知识分子的良知与勇气。他的修辞学技巧和哲学思想成为西方人文主义传统的重要组成部分。
supporter.en: Cicero is revered as one of Rome's greatest orators, philosophers, and statesmen. He defended the republican system against dictatorship and laid the foundation for Rome's legal tradition. He introduced Greek philosophical thought to Rome, creating a Latin philosophical language that preserved Western civilization. His works 'De Re Publica' and 'De Legibus' became classics of political theory, influencing countless later thinkers. Cicero maintained his moral principles and independent thinking even during political crises, embodying the conscience and courage of intellectuals. His rhetorical skills and philosophical thought became essential components of the Western humanist tradition.

critic.zh: 批评者认为西塞罗过于理想主义，政治判断力不足。他在内战中摇摆不定，最终未能阻止共和国的崩溃。作为'新人'(novus homo)，他渴望贵族认可，有时表现出政治机会主义。他的哲学思想被批评为缺乏原创性，主要是对希腊哲学的编译和通俗化。此外，西塞罗在处理喀提林阴谋时未经审判处死公民，违背了他所倡导的法治原则。他的政治生涯充满矛盾，既维护共和又与独裁者妥协，反映了罗马共和国晚期政治道德的衰落。
critic.en: Critics argue that Cicero was too idealistic and lacked political judgment. He vacillated during the civil wars and ultimately failed to prevent the collapse of the republic. As a 'new man' (novus homo), he craved aristocratic approval and sometimes displayed political opportunism. His philosophical thought is criticized for lacking originality, being primarily a compilation and popularization of Greek philosophy. Additionally, Cicero's execution of citizens without trial during the Catilinarian conspiracy contradicted the legal principles he advocated. His political career was full of contradictions, defending the republic while compromising with dictators, reflecting the decline of political morality in the late Roman Republic.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，西塞罗被视为罗马共和国晚期最重要的知识分子和政治人物。他既是政治实践者，也是思想传播者，在罗马从共和向帝国转变的关键时期发挥了重要作用。他的著作成为连接希腊罗马文化的桥梁，影响了西方法治思想和政治理论的发展。西塞罗的生平反映了罗马共和国末期的政治危机和道德困境，他的悲剧性结局象征着共和理想的失败。现代学者研究西塞罗不仅关注他的政治生涯，也重视他作为文化中介者的角色，以及他对拉丁文学语言的贡献。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Cicero is regarded as the most important intellectual and political figure of the late Roman Republic. He was both a political practitioner and a disseminator of ideas, playing a crucial role during Rome's transition from republic to empire. His works became a bridge between Greek and Roman cultures, influencing the development of Western legal thought and political theory. Cicero's life reflects the political crisis and moral dilemma of the late Roman Republic, and his tragic fate symbolizes the failure of republican ideals. Modern scholars study Cicero not only for his political career but also for his role as a cultural intermediary and his contributions to the Latin literary language.

self.zh: 自由不是做你想做的事，而是有权做你应该做的事。
self.en: Freedom is not the power of doing what we like, but the right to be able to do what we ought.

others.zh: 西塞罗的舌头比他的剑更令罗马元老院恐惧。
others.en: Cicero's tongue was more feared in the Roman Senate than any sword.
